## Self-review pass 2 — `unknown{executor_error}` root cause (2026-11-04)

**Verdict: a DISTINCT defect — not the probe/journal gap surfacing
earlier.** Reproduced deterministically (3/3) with journaled stderr
captured through the helper's own `read` journal:

- **Exec-path defect (new machinery finding):** `hh-helper`'s `Hello`
  dispatch (`crates/hh-helper/src/server.rs:185-191`) re-derives
  `srv.backend = "seatbelt"` whenever the hello carries a containment
  policy AND `seatbelt::is_available()` — silently discarding the
  spawned `--backend podman` (`container`) declaration (present since
  S2.1 `27fed3f2`). On this host (seatbelt + podman both live) every
  contained `Exec` therefore runs host-side under the seatbelt profile.
  Verbatim evidence: cell stderr `cat: /proc/mounts: No such file or
  directory`, `/usr/bin/grep: Operation not permitted`, `ls: /work: No
  such file or directory`, `/bin/sh: /work/submission.json: No such
  file or directory` → child exit 1 → `ToolError{ExecutorError}` →
  declared class → compensable effect → `OutcomeMap::Unknown{
  executor_error}` (dispatch.rs:3685-3700). The session's hello reply
  itself reports `backend:"seatbelt"` — recorded verbatim in the
  packet's `executor_backend` fact. The same `podman exec` run
  directly against the identical container/mount succeeds (exit 0), and
  the real helper+socket exchange succeeds when hello carries no policy.
  Corollary (honesty): any earlier "podman lane" exec with a policy
  attached took the same seatbelt path — podman exec was never actually
  exercised end-to-end before this run.
- **Probe ENOENT mechanism refined (the carried predicate):**
  `HelperExecutor::probe` → `HelperClient::connect` (helper.rs:218-243)
  → socket connect + `try_clone` succeed (socket persists on the podman
  lane) → **`Command::new("/bin/true").spawn()` — the placeholder
  child — fails ENOENT**: this host has `/usr/bin/true`, no `/bin/true`
  (verified: `ls /bin/true` → No such file; a minimal spawn repro
  prints the verbatim `No such file or directory (os error 2)`). So the
  GATE-G11-recorded mechanism ("journal/exec-record resolution not
  live") is one step too deep: the verb never reaches the helper —
  `connect` dies at the placeholder spawn before any hello. (Design
  note: `serve()` also serializes connections, so a same-process probe
  reconnect cannot be served while the session channel is open — the
  verb is architecturally a post-kernel-loss resume path.)
- **Disposition:** both defects stay unresolved — the honest
  `inconclusive{dispatch_outcome:unknown:executor_error}` legs are the
  designed output, never forced to `observed:applied`. The probe repair
  stays the GATE-G11 carried predicate (`probe_verb_enoent`); the
  clobber is recorded as a second carried predicate
  (`exec_backend_hello_clobber`), both verbatim in the packet.
- **Pass-2 corrections to the battery (honest folds, not forced):**
  `SubjectOutcome.executor_backend` recorded verbatim; `controls`
  decoupled from subject artifacts (instrument-side — now `verified`
  through the real adapter); `AdapterOracle` sends the adapter's own
  fixture `task_id` (the committed binary resolves only fixture ids —
  corpus semantic ids are a different record identity → `UnknownTask` →
  `oracle_failure`; fixed); `join.attempt_rows_join` and
  `submission_digest_matches` no longer vacuously pass on absent
  members (`refused` names the missing member); cross-test container
  residue swept honestly (`hh-env-*` leaks from SIGKILLed helpers);
  live assertions assert the typed verdict of the honest outcome.
- **Executed packet:** `docs/build/reports/2026-11-04-r5.43-s1-useful.json`
  — subject_a/b `inconclusive{dispatch_outcome:unknown:executor_error}`
  (`executor_backend:"seatbelt"`, probe verbatim), oracle_chain
  `inconclusive{oracle_not_attempted:subjects}`, controls `verified`,

  `refused{join:submission_digest}`, worksheet `verified`, disposition
